news.headline: Uniqure (QURE) Total Assets 2025: $824.9M, up 48.2%
news.summary: uniQure ended fiscal 2025 with total assets of $824.9 million, up 48.2% year over year, reflecting the buildup of cash and investments ahead of the AMT-130 regulatory filings and planned commercial launch.

news.headline: Uniqure (QURE) Free Cash Flow 2025: $178.4M outflow, up 4.1%
news.summary: uniQure burned $178.4 million in free cash flow in fiscal 2025, a 4.1% increase in outflow versus the prior year, as R&D and pre-commercial spending on AMT-130 ramped ahead of the BLA submission.

news.headline: uniQure Shares Fall Despite AMT-130 Filing as William Blair Resumes Coverage at Outperform
news.summary: William Blair resumed coverage with an Outperform rating and $73 fair-value estimate (about 58% implied upside), calling BLA acceptance the next incremental catalyst, yet QURE shares still fell roughly 4-5% on profit-taking, insider-selling concerns and lingering uncertainty over whether regulators will require costly confirmatory studies. Analysts noted the parallel UK filing could position AMT-130 for approval in two countries in 2027.

news.headline: uniQure Announces Submission of Biologics License Application for AMT-130 in Huntington's Disease
news.summary: uniQure submitted a Biologics License Application to the FDA seeking accelerated approval of ifezuntirgene inilparvovec (AMT-130), backed by 3-year Phase I/II data showing a 75% slowing of disease progression on cUHDRS versus matched controls, and simultaneously filed a Marketing Authorisation Application with the UK's MHRA. The company requested FDA priority review, which if granted could set an approval action date around late April/early May 2027, marking the first-ever regulatory filing for a Huntington's disease gene therapy.

news.headline: Wells Fargo Raises uniQure Price Target to $75 from $60
news.summary: Wells Fargo lifted its price target on QURE following the Q2 update, citing growing confidence in the AMT-130 accelerated-approval pathway after the FDA agreed the 3-year dataset could support a BLA, adding to a string of bullish analyst revisions ahead of the Q3 filing.

news.headline: uniQure Announces Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Provides Company Update
news.summary: uniQure reported Q2 revenue of $5.8 million (+9.4% YoY) and cash, equivalents and investments of $810.3 million (up from $622.5 million at year-end 2025) after a $259 million share offering, extending its runway into 2030; net loss widened to $81.1 million. Management reaffirmed plans to submit the AMT-130 BLA and UK MAA in Q3 2026 and reported encouraging early biologic-activity signals from the AMT-260 epilepsy program.

catalysts.label: AMT-130 four-year Phase I/II topline data
catalysts.detail: uniQure plans to report four-year safety and efficacy data (12 high-dose and 12 low-dose patients, plus additional 3-year high-dose patients) from the pivotal Phase I/II study in Huntington's disease, including cUHDRS and CSF neurofilament light chain trends benchmarked against a natural history cohort. Considered a key readout that could reinforce the BLA and MAA filings.

catalysts.label: FDA 60-day BLA filing/priority-review determination
catalysts.detail: Following the September 2, 2026 BLA submission, the FDA has a standard 60-day filing review period during which it decides whether to accept the application and whether to grant the requested priority review, which would compress the subsequent review to about six months.

catalysts.label: Potential FDA accelerated-approval action date
catalysts.detail: If the FDA accepts the BLA and grants priority review, analysts estimate an action date around late April to early May 2027 for a decision on accelerated approval of AMT-130, which would be the first disease-modifying treatment for Huntington's disease.

catalysts.label: UK MHRA marketing authorisation review
catalysts.detail: uniQure filed a Marketing Authorisation Application for AMT-130 with the UK's MHRA on September 2, 2026, following a positive pre-submission meeting and use of the Innovative Licensing and Access Pathway (ILAP); a decision could position the UK as a parallel launch market alongside the US in 2027.

catalysts.label: Possible FDA Advisory Committee (AdCom) meeting
catalysts.detail: Management indicated on the Q2 2026 call that an FDA advisory committee meeting is likely before a final decision on the AMT-130 BLA; timing has not been set but would typically occur during the review cycle.

catalysts.label: AMT-260 second dose-cohort enrollment complete (epilepsy)
catalysts.detail: uniQure expects to complete enrollment of the second, higher dose cohort in the Phase I/IIa trial of AMT-260 for refractory mesial temporal lobe epilepsy in Q3 2026, following early low-dose data showing seizure reductions of 79-100% in 3 of 6 patients.

catalysts.label: AMT-260 updated Phase I/IIa data (epilepsy)
catalysts.detail: Updated results from the Phase I/IIa AMT-260 epilepsy study, including data from the second dose cohort, are expected in the first half of 2027.

catalysts.label: Q3 2026 earnings report
catalysts.detail: uniQure's next quarterly financial results and corporate update are expected around early November 2026, based on the company's historical reporting cadence; likely to update on BLA/MAA filing status and cash runway.

catalysts.label: Potential AMT-130 commercial launch (US/UK)
catalysts.detail: If accelerated approval and/or UK marketing authorisation are granted, uniQure has said it is preparing commercial infrastructure and has engaged Huntington's Disease Centers of Excellence and payers, targeting a possible launch in 2027 in one or both markets.

catalysts.label: Additional AMT-191 (Fabry disease) clinical data
catalysts.detail: uniQure continues dosing and follow-up in the Phase I/IIa trial of AMT-191 for Fabry disease after pausing mid/high-dose administration in early 2026 following Grade 3 liver enzyme elevations in two patients; further safety and efficacy updates are expected as the program resumes, with no confirmed BLA timeline yet.

pulse: QURE trades in the mid-$40s (roughly $45-47 in early September 2026), down from a 52-week high near $71.50 but well above 2025 lows, after the stock sold off modestly even as the company hit its most important milestone in years: the September 2, 2026 submission of a BLA (with requested priority review) and a parallel UK MHRA filing for AMT-130 in Huntington's disease, based on 3-year data showing a 75% slowing of disease progression. Sentiment is broadly bullish - Wall Street consensus is Strong Buy with price targets clustering in the $65-95 range (Wells Fargo $75, William Blair fair value $73) - but the stock's dip on filing day reflects lingering risk that regulators could still demand confirmatory studies or reject the filing, alongside routine insider selling after the year's sharp rally; a $259M June equity raise has pushed cash to $810 million and runway into 2030. The next catalysts to watch are the four-year AMT-130 topline data due this September, the FDA's 60-day filing/priority-review decision expected around November 2026, and any signal on a possible FDA advisory committee meeting ahead of a potential accelerated-approval action date around April-May 2027.
